issues.context: ZCG (Zcash Community Grants) gets 8% of block rewards via the Development Fund, which expires in November 2028. Proposals would end, shrink or keep that stream.
issues.question: Should ZCG keep receiving a share of each block reward?

stances.description: Stop ZCG's funding stream, with the money going to the NSM or elsewhere.
stances.label: End it

stances.description: Reduce the stream or treasury so ZCG continues on less, with the rest going elsewhere.
stances.label: Shrink it as a compromise

stances.description: Continue the funding, but restructure how ZCG is run and held accountable.
stances.label: Keep it, reform ZCG

issues.context: Today ZCG, a grants committee, directs part of the Development Fund, and coinholders vote on the rest. Threads disagree on who should hold that decision, and how.
issues.question: Who should decide how block-reward grant money is spent?

stances.description: Those who bear the cost decide, with votes counted by coins held.
stances.label: Coin-weighted holder vote

stances.description: Add per-person polling so coin amounts alone do not decide.
stances.label: Per-person holder polling

stances.description: A standing committee with clear goals, named managers and oversight.
stances.label: An accountable grants body

stances.description: End the fund; holders and businesses can pay for work directly.
stances.label: No shared fund at all

issues.context: ZCG closed its vulnerability bounty over report volume, which AI has made cheap to produce. Threads debate keeping a redesigned bounty or ending the standing program.
issues.question: Should Zcash keep paying rewards for security vulnerability reports?

stances.description: Keep rewarding valid reports, with tighter scope, proof checks, dedicated triage or a bond.
stances.label: Keep a bounty, redesigned

stances.description: Close it; responsible disclosure continues, with discretionary rewards for critical finds.
stances.label: No standing bounty

issues.context: ZCG funded outreach such as ZECsy, which onboards people who need private payments; a draft ZIP would aim ZCG grants at getting ZEC into new users' hands.
issues.question: Should shared grant funds back outreach aimed at particular social causes or groups?

stances.description: Grants may reach any lawful group that needs private payments; adoption is the goal.
stances.label: Yes, if lawful and adds users

stances.description: Shared money should serve Zcash broadly, not particular causes; charity should be opt-in.
stances.label: No, keep funds broadly useful

issues.context: Some wallets route swaps through services like NEAR Intents, which run compliance checks on incoming ZEC and can hold funds while a review is open.
issues.question: Should Zcash wallets offer swaps through services that can screen and hold funds?

stances.description: Checks on ZEC leaving the shielded pool are reasonable, and users can help clear a hold.
stances.label: Yes, screening is normal

stances.description: Acceptable if the wallet tells users in the app, before use, that funds can be restricted.
stances.label: Yes, with clear warnings

stances.description: Favor swaps that no one can stop or freeze over services that screen and may hold funds.
stances.label: No, only freeze-proof swaps
